## Data requirements

`data/` is not committed (it is gitignored because of its size). Before running this
document, download the following into `data/`:

1. **WorldClim 2.1 bioclimatic variables, 30 arc-second resolution** (Fick & Hijmans 2017).
   Download `wc2.1_30s_bio.zip` from <https://www.worldclim.org/data/worldclim21.html>
   (direct link: <https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/climate/worldclim/2_1/base/wc2.1_30s_bio.zip>)
   and unzip it into `data/wc2.1_30s_bio/`. This document uses BIO1 and BIO12;
   `Analysis.qmd` also uses BIO5 and BIO10.
2. **AusTraits v7.0.0** (Falster et al. 2021, <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3568417>).
   Save the release's `.rds` file as `data/austraits-7.0.0.rds`, either by downloading it
   from Zenodo or with `austraits::load_austraits(version = "7.0.0", path = "data")`.

Files already committed in `data-processed/` and used here:

- `australia.tif`: Australia mask used to crop the climate rasters.
- `datasets_with_leaf_area_edited.csv`: hand-annotated compound-leaf filter (Step 5).
- `data_traits_climate.parquet`: the output of this document. The dataset is only
  rebuilt if this file is absent, so delete it to rebuild from AusTraits.

## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(terra) # used to extract and process rasters
```

```{r}
# Create folders this document writes to (data/ is gitignored, so they don't exist in a fresh clone)
for (dir in c("data/leaf_compound_filter", "data-processed")) {
  dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
```


## Get climate covariates

Load climate covariates from worldclim

- BIO_1: "Annual Mean Temperature" — the average temperature (°C) over the year for a location.
- BIO_12 is a bioclimatic variable representing "Annual Precipitation." 


```{r}
# Select the two WorldClim bioclimate raster files to load:
#   BIO_1  = Annual Mean Temperature
#   BIO_12 = Annual Precipitation
vars <- c("wc2.1_30s_bio_1.tif", "wc2.1_30s_bio_12.tif")

# Load the Australia boundary raster (used as a crop mask)
australia <- terra::rast("data-processed/australia.tif")

# Load both climate rasters, stack them, and crop to the Australian extent
stacked_rasters <-
  file.path("data/wc2.1_30s_bio", vars) |>
  terra::rast() |>
  terra::crop(australia)
```

## AusTraits

```{r}
# Traits of interest for the analysis
traits <- c(
  "leaf_mass_per_area", "leaf_area",
  "leaf_N_per_area",
  "wood_density", "leaf_delta13C",
  "huber_value","photosynthetic_pathway","leaflet_area","seed_dry_mass"
)

output <- "data-processed/data_traits_climate.parquet"

# Only build the dataset if the output file doesn't already exist (cache check)
if (!file.exists(output)) {
  # --- Step 1: Load and flatten the AusTraits database ---
  # Reads the raw nested RDS and flattens it into a single tidy data frame
  austraits_unflattened <- readRDS("data/austraits-7.0.0.rds")

  austraits <- austraits_unflattened |>
    austraits::flatten_database()
  # --- Step 2: Filter to field observations with valid coordinates ---
  # Keeps only:
  #   - traits of interest
  #   - all field records
  #   - field_experiment records only when they are:
  #     * Crous_2019 or Firn_2019 with treatment_context_id == "01"
  #     * Auld_2000 seed_dry_mass records
  #   - observations that have both latitude and longitude

  austraits_geo <-
    austraits |>
    filter(
      trait_name %in% traits,
      basis_of_record %in% c("field") | (basis_of_record %in% c("field_experiment") &
                                           ((dataset_id %in% c("Crous_2019","Firn_2019") &
                                             treatment_context_id == "01") |
                                            (dataset_id == "Auld_2000" &
                                             trait_name == "seed_dry_mass"))),
      !is.na(`latitude (deg)`), !is.na(`longitude (deg)`)
    ) |>
    mutate(across(c("latitude (deg)", "longitude (deg)", value), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) |>
    # Drop rows where coordinate conversion produced NAs
    filter(
      !is.na(`latitude (deg)`), !is.na(`longitude (deg)`)
    )
    
  # --- Step 3: Build a lookup table for leaf compoundness per species ---
  # Classifies each species as "compound" if it ever has compound leaves,
  # or "simple" otherwise. Used later to filter leaf area measurements.
  austraits|>
  filter(trait_name == "leaf_compoundness")|>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(num_types = n_distinct(value)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(compoundness = if_else(num_types > 1 | value =="compound" | value == "compound simple", "compound", "simple")) |>
  dplyr::select(-value) |>
  distinct(taxon_name, .keep_all = T) |>
  dplyr::select(compoundness, taxon_name) -> compound_taxa
  
  # --- Step 4: Flag leaf_area datasets that contain compound-leaved species ---
  # Exports a CSV for manual review so datasets can be annotated with what leaf
  # unit was actually measured (whole leaf vs. leaflet).
  austraits_geo |>
  filter(trait_name == "leaf_area") |>
  left_join(compound_taxa) |> 
  group_by(dataset_id) |>
  mutate(compound_species = if_else(any(is.na(compoundness)) |any(compoundness == "compound") , "compound_present","no_compound")) |>
  distinct(dataset_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(dataset_id, compound_species) |>
  ungroup()|>
  mutate(leaf_unit_measured = NA,
         evidence = NA,
         notes = NA) %>%
  write_csv("data/leaf_compound_filter/datasets_with_leaf_area.csv")
  
  # --- Step 5: Apply the manually edited compound-leaf filter ---
  # Read back the hand-annotated CSV and remove leaf_area records where the
  # dataset measured individual leaves but the species is compound (i.e. the
  # measurement reflects a leaflet, not a whole leaf).
  datasets_with_leaf_area <- read_csv("data-processed/datasets_with_leaf_area_edited.csv")
  
  austraits_geo |>
    filter(trait_name %in% c("leaf_area")) |>
    left_join(datasets_with_leaf_area) -> austraits_geo_leaf_area

  austraits_geo_leaf_area |>
  left_join(compound_taxa) |>
  # Will also remove compound species observations when unclear what leaf unit was measured
  filter(!(compound_species == "compound_present" & leaf_unit_measured == "leaf" & compoundness %in% c(NA,"compound"))) |>
  dplyr::select(-compound_species, -leaf_unit_measured, -evidence, -notes, -compoundness) -> austraits_geo_leaf_area_compound_removed
  
  # Recombine filtered leaf_area rows with all other traits.
  # Also relabel "leaflet_area" as "leaf_area" so the trait name is consistent.
  austraits_geo |>
  filter(!trait_name %in% c("leaf_area")) |>
  bind_rows(austraits_geo_leaf_area_compound_removed) |>
  mutate(trait_name = ifelse(trait_name == "leaflet_area","leaf_area",trait_name)) -> austraits_geo

  # --- Step 6: Remove non-C3 observations from leaf_delta13C ---
  # δ13C is only a meaningful water-use efficiency proxy for C3 plants.
  # Strategy:
  #   (a) Build a per-species photosynthetic pathway lookup from all AusTraits records,
  #       restricted to species with a single unambiguous reported pathway.
  #   (b) Drop leaf_delta13C rows where the pathway is KNOWN and not "c3".
  #   (c) Retain leaf_delta13C rows with NA pathway (species not in the lookup),
  #       but drop those with value > -20 ‰ — values this enriched are implausible
  #       for C3 and most likely represent C4 or CAM individuals.
  austraits |>
    filter(trait_name == "photosynthetic_pathway") |>
    dplyr::select(taxon_name, value) |>
    group_by(taxon_name) |>
    nest(photosynthetic_pathway = -taxon_name) |>
    mutate(photosynthetic_pathway = map(photosynthetic_pathway, ~unique(.x$value))) |>
    mutate(length_pathways = map_dbl(photosynthetic_pathway, ~length(.x))) |>
    filter(length_pathways == 1) |>   # keep only species with a single reported pathway
    unnest(photosynthetic_pathway) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(taxon_name, photosynthetic_pathway) -> c3_c4_identity

  austraits_geo |>
    left_join(c3_c4_identity, by = "taxon_name") |>
    filter(
      # (b) Remove delta13C rows with a known non-C3 pathway
      !(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C" & !is.na(photosynthetic_pathway) & photosynthetic_pathway != "c3"),
      # (c) Remove delta13C rows with unknown pathway but value > -20 ‰
      !(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C" & is.na(photosynthetic_pathway) & as.numeric(value) > -20)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-photosynthetic_pathway) -> austraits_geo
  
  # --- Step 7: Extract climate values at each observation's coordinates ---
  # Convert the trait data frame to a spatial vector (points) and extract
  # temperature and precipitation from the stacked WorldClim rasters.
  # The raster cell index is also retained to identify co-located observations.
  trait_data_vect <-
    austraits_geo |>
    select("longitude (deg)", "latitude (deg)") |>
    terra::vect(
      geom = c("longitude (deg)", "latitude (deg)"),
      crs = terra::crs(stacked_rasters)
    )

  data_traits_climate <-
    terra::extract(x = stacked_rasters, y = trait_data_vect, method = "simple", bind = TRUE, xy = FALSE, cells = TRUE, ID = FALSE, dataframe = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    bind_cols(austraits_geo) |>
    rename(decimal_longitude = `longitude (deg)`, decimal_latitude = `latitude (deg)`, annual_precipitation = wc2.1_30s_bio_12, average_temperature = wc2.1_30s_bio_1) |>
    select(decimal_longitude, decimal_latitude, annual_precipitation, average_temperature, everything())

  # --- Step 8: Join species life-history (annual/perennial) from Wenk_2023 ---
  # Concatenates multiple recorded values per species into a single string.
  species_life_history <-
  austraits_unflattened |>
  austraits::extract_dataset("Wenk_2023") |>
  austraits::extract_trait("life_history") |>
  pluck("traits") |>
  select(taxon_name, life_history = value) |>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
    mutate(life_history = paste0(life_history, collapse = " ")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct()
  
  # --- Step 9: Join species growth form from Wenk_2022 and simplify categories ---
  # Derives two new columns:
  #   woody        : broad binary split (woody vs. non-woody)
  #   growth_form_simpler : collapsed into 6 coarse categories
  species_growth_form <-
  austraits_unflattened |>
  austraits::extract_dataset("Wenk_2022") |>
  austraits::extract_trait("growth_form") |>
  pluck("traits") |>
  select(taxon_name, growth_form = value) |>
  distinct()|>
    mutate(
      woody = ifelse(
        !str_detect(growth_form, "herb|fern|tussock|geophyte|lycophyte|basal_large|graminoid|hummock"), "woody", "non-woody"
      )
    )|>
    select(-growth_form) |>
  distinct()
  
  # --- Step 10: Attach life-history and growth-form, then write final dataset ---
  # Saves the complete dataset as a Parquet file for efficient downstream use.
  data_traits_climate <- data_traits_climate |>
    left_join(by = "taxon_name", species_life_history) |>
    left_join(by = "taxon_name", species_growth_form)
    
  # data_traits_climate_woody_NA <- data_traits_climate |> 
  #   filter(is.na(woody))
  # write_csv(data_traits_climate_woody_NA, "data/leaf_compound_filter/data_traits_climate_woody_NA.csv")
  
  data_traits_climate |>
    arrow::write_parquet("data-processed/data_traits_climate.parquet")
}

```
